snapshot.label: Snapshot 006
snapshot.scope: Kempsey Shire Council terminology encountered in Council webpages, planning material, policies, meeting records, contribution registers, procurement material, corporate plans, annual/statutory reporting, financial statements, capital works, disaster-recovery records, emergency-management material, development-assessment workflow guidance, water/sewer project material and supporting NSW local-government sources used only where necessary to resolve KSC-used codes.
snapshot.method: Terms are preserved as encountered. Expansions are recorded only where supported. Unresolved codes remain unresolved rather than being guessed.
snapshot.status: Cumulative through Sweep 006. Snapshots 001, 002, 003, 004 and 005 remain frozen and are not overwritten. Further research passes will continue as separately numbered DOCX snapshots.

classificationRules.meaning: Appears in historical KSC material but has been superseded, renamed or replaced.
NSW Government, Commonwealth or industry terminology used by KSC.
Code or abbreviation is demonstrably used, but its literal expansion has not yet been established from an authoritative source.
Meaning depends on context and requires disambiguation.

items: Expanded current KSC policy-control architecture using the Policy Framework Policy and current procedure documents.
Added current procurement shorthand and platform terminology from KSC tender/procurement material.
Added corporate and financial terminology evidenced in KSC planning and Long-Term Financial Plan material.
Added engineering and standards shorthand encountered in KSC planning and procurement sources.
Confirmed TQE remains a current KSC procurement identifier family; its literal expansion remains unresolved.
Recorded KSC policy Document Number examples without inferring the meaning of their prefixes.
Incorporated the A-to-G block of the official Kempsey Development Control Plan 2026 Appendix 1, Table E.1 abbreviation/acronym glossary.
Flagged two material KSC terminology collisions: CMP = Coastal Management Program or Conservation Management Plan depending on context; BCA and BCA 2016 refer to different instruments.
Added meeting-record shorthand and identifier syntax including Cr, Clr, KDCP, FNA, ERSA, Council File Number family FYY/####[/##], and resolution identifiers YYYY.NN(N).
Added further legacy CPOL and procedure identifiers cited in the 2013 DCP, without treating historical references as proof of current policy status.
Reclassified F22/1933 as part of an evidenced KSC F-year File/Document Number family while leaving the literal meaning of the leading F unresolved.

DCP Appendix 1 terminology was checked against KSC’s current DCP page and an indexed HTML rendering of Part E. The KSC Part E PDF endpoint could not be fetched by the research environment, so that access limitation is recorded rather than concealed.

Added KSC water and sewer management terminology from the Water Supply Asset Management Plan, Drinking Water Management System material, current water-service pages and the Water and Sewer Equivalent Tenement Determination Procedure.
Added current development-processing shorthand and identifiers including REFDA, RFI and s4.55(2) modification notation.
Added current corporate action-code families from the Delivery Program 2025-2029 and Operational Plan architecture: EN.DP#, EC.DP#, CO.DP#, LE.DP# and the corresponding OP-code families.
Added governance and emergency-management shorthand including ELT, LEMC and HM CRG, where KSC sources support the expansion.

Expanded the register with legacy asset-management abbreviations that remain useful when reading older KSC infrastructure records, while marking them LEGACY rather than silently treating them as current.
TQE, T6, LD and the leading F in F-year file numbers remain unresolved; no unsupported expansions were introduced.

KSC PDF screenshots were attempted for key water-management documents during source verification but the web cache could not return the raster pages. Extracted indexed text and current KSC webpages were retained as the evidentiary basis, and the access limitation is recorded rather than concealed.

Harvested KSC’s formal “Key Abbreviations” table from the Delivery Program and Operational Plan 2022-2026, adding previously missing Council-defined terms including AFZ, E&ESD, JO, MIDWASTE, MNC, NAIDOC, NCA, PID, PAMP, RFS, TfNSW and WAP.

Harvested the capital-project abbreviation table embedded in the 2024-25 Delivery Program / Operational Plan, adding project, fund, holiday-park, road-class and infrastructure codes including ASM, CHHP, CLIRP, HBHP, HHHP, LRCIP, LRCIRC, MH, PLC, RAP, RTAF, SDC, SF, SPHP, SRR, SRRL, SWR, UR, URL, URR, WF and WTS.

Recorded an internal KSC source collision: the 2024-25 capital-project appendix assigns URR both "Unsealed Rural Roads" and "Urban Roads Regional". The glossary preserves both and marks URR AMBIGUOUS rather than silently correcting the source.

Expanded current financial and statutory-reporting terminology from the 2024-25 Annual Report and audited financial statements, including AASB, CAPEX, CALD, EEO, FDR, FTE, GPFS, IPPE, KMP, NCP, SPFS and UCV.
Added financial-sustainability and funding shorthand used in KSC’s Long-Term Financial Plan: FSP, FAG and R2R.
Resolved AGRN as Australian Government Reference Number using KSC project coding together with the NSW Government disaster-declaration framework.
Resolved LTREWS as Long-term Renewable Energy and Water Strategy by cross-reading KSC’s Environmental Levy project label with the strategy title in Council’s Community Strategic Plan.

Added current work-order architecture: W#### is explicitly labelled by KSC as a Work order number. Embedded DM##### and G#####-## subcodes are preserved as observed but remain UNRESOLVED pending authoritative KSC document-control definitions.

Harvested KSC’s Development Application Status Guide and recorded the exact public workflow vocabulary used from REFDA submission through assessment, peer review, Council determination and final completion states. The glossary now distinguishes a rejected intake application from a refused assessed application and records Public Exhibition as a status that can overlap another displayed status.

Resolved DM##### beyond its previous UNRESOLVED state. KSC embeds DM numbers in current disaster-recovery work orders; NSW local-government disaster-recovery material independently defines DM-prefixed identifiers as Damage Numbers tied to specific project locations. The resolution is recorded as cross-council corroboration rather than attributed to an express KSC expansion.

Expanded emergency-management terminology with LEMO, LEOCON and EOC from KSC material, plus historical DISPLAN and EASP terminology used in KSC coastal emergency-planning material. Period-specific status is retained so legacy emergency terminology is not silently treated as current.

Upgraded procurement architecture using KSC’s current Government Contracts register. The register explicitly labels its field "Tender Number (TQE)", confirming TQE as a tender-number family while still not revealing the literal words represented by the letters. PO###### is also recorded as a current observed procurement/contract identifier family with its prefix expansion left unresolved.

Added GIPAA as a KSC-used shorthand variant for the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009 alongside the already-recorded "GIPA Act" form. Source-form preservation is required because KSC uses both.

Expanded current water, sewer and infrastructure shorthand with SMD WTP, NWG, D&C and K&G, then harvested KSC Standard Drawing ASD 203 for the formal street-name abbreviation layer: ST, ESP, RD, CR, CL, TCE, PL, CT, DR, GR, AV, LA, PDE and BVD. The CR/Cr collision is explicitly flagged.

Added current and historical emergency/public-agency shorthand including NSW SES, ADF and BoM where directly evidenced in KSC material, while retaining the period and functional context of each source.

Preserved G#####-## as UNRESOLVED. Repeated KSC use confirms it is an embedded project/grant-style code family, but this sweep did not locate authoritative material defining the literal G prefix or number-allocation scheme.

referenceSections.title: Corporate performance action-code architecture — Sweep 004
items: Current Delivery Program 2025-2029 families: EN.DP# = Environment; EC.DP# = Economy; CO.DP# = Community; LE.DP# = Leadership.
Operational Plan actions use corresponding OP families: EN.OP#, EC.OP#, CO.OP# and LE.OP#.
The number identifies the individual action within the thematic family. These codes are evidence-traceable identifiers and should be preserved verbatim in extracts and investigation registers.
Operational-plan code sets are annual implementation codes beneath the four-year Delivery Program; an OP code therefore must be read with the applicable financial-year Operational Plan.

referenceSections.title: Development processing identifiers — Sweep 004
items: REFDA###### is the initial reference identifier used by KSC after submission through the NSW Planning Portal, before the application completes intake processing.
DA######## is the later development-application identifier family already recorded in this glossary.
RFI is a process status/document shorthand, not an application-number family.
s4.55(2) identifies a statutory modification pathway and can appear beside an existing DA number and revision suffix.

referenceSections.title: Development application status vocabulary — Sweep 006
items: KSC’s Development Application Status Guide uses the following exact public workflow labels. These are process-state terms, not interchangeable outcome labels:
Submitted — application received through the NSW Planning Portal and carrying a REFDA reference.
Under Intake Review — initial completeness/intake checking.
Processing Payment — fees are being prepared/processed.
Awaiting Payment — payment is required before progression.
Payment Received — payment has been received.
Queued for Assessment — application is waiting to be assigned/assessed.
External Referral — application is with an external referral body or authority.
Ready for Assessment — intake/referral prerequisites have progressed to assessment readiness.
RFI Requested — Request for Information issued; further information is required.
Assigned — application has been allocated to an assessing officer.
Under Assessment — substantive assessment is occurring.
Peer Review — assessment is undergoing internal peer review.
Council Meeting for Determination — matter is proceeding to a Council meeting for determination.
Ready for Issue — determination/documentation is prepared for issue.
Complete – Approved — completed with approval.
Complete – Refused — completed following substantive refusal.
Complete – Rejected — rejected at the intake/acceptance stage; this is not the same as refusal and a new DA is required.
Complete – Withdrawn — completed because the application was withdrawn.
Public Exhibition — application is on exhibition; KSC notes this status may occur while another status is also relevant.
referenceSections.note: Source: KSC Development Application Status Guide (kempsey.nsw.gov.au, /Plan-Build/Development-applications/Lodge-your-DA/Development-Application-Status-Guide).

referenceSections.title: Work-order and embedded project-code architecture — cumulative through Sweep 006
items: W#### = KSC work-order number family, explicitly evidenced by the "Work order no. and Description" column in Operational Plans.

DM##### = Damage Number family used in KSC disaster-recovery work orders. The literal expansion is resolved through current NSW local-government disaster-recovery corroboration; KSC use is direct, while the spelled-out meaning comes from the corroborating NSW council source.
G#####-## = embedded current project/grant-style subcode observed inside KSC work-order descriptions. Literal expansion and allocation scheme remain unresolved.
AGRN#### = Australian Government Reference Number identifying a declared natural-disaster event; this identifier has been independently resolved from the NSW disaster-declaration framework.

referenceSections.title: Identifier architecture observed
items: YYYY/LD-##### — Former development-record identifier family. Literal internal meaning of LD remains unresolved.
T6-YY-### — Separate legacy KSC development/application identifier family. Literal meaning of T6 remains unresolved.
DA######## — Newer development-application identifier architecture used by Council.
PP-YYYY-#### — Planning Proposal identifier architecture.
MP##_#### — NSW Major Project identifier architecture rather than an ordinary KSC DA identifier.

TQE##/## or TQE##-## — Tender-number reference architecture. KSC’s current Government Contracts register labels the field "Tender Number (TQE)", confirming the function of the identifier. Literal expansion of the letters TQE remains unresolved.
PO###### — Current procurement/contract identifier family observed in the same KSC Government Contracts register field as TQE numbers. Prefix expansion remains unresolved.
REV / REV01 / REV02 ... — Revision suffix architecture.
Meeting item 11.4 / 11.4.1 etc. — Hierarchical agenda and attachment numbering used in Council meeting packages.

referenceSections.title: Current policy document-control architecture — cumulative through Sweep 003
items: Current KSC policies use structured Document Control fields including Title, Policy Number, Version, Document Number, Audience, Policy Type, Category, Subcategory, approval/effective/review dates, Responsible Officer, Approval Body, consultation requirements and Version Control.
Observed current policy identifiers include Policy 5.11 / Version 4 / Document Number D24/73553 and Policy 5.9 / Version 5 / Document Number F22/1933.

KSC formally distinguishes Council Policies from Operational Policies. Council Policies have an external focus and are adopted or revised by the governing body; Operational Policies have an internal focus and are adopted or revised by the General Manager or delegate.
Procedures use hierarchical identifiers under a parent policy, evidenced by Procedure 2.1.4 under Policy 2.1 and Procedure 5.1.3 under Policy 5.1.
The literal meanings of the D24 and F22 Document Number prefixes have not been established. No prefix expansion is inferred.

referenceSections.title: Collision recap (terms already detailed above, flagged again for visibility)
items: CMP — KSC uses CMP for both Coastal Management Program and Conservation Management Plan. Never expand CMP without identifying the source context.
BCA / BCA 2016 — In the KSC DCP glossary, BCA means Building Code of Australia, while "BCA 2016" means Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016. The year qualifier is therefore material, not cosmetic.
Cr / Clr — Current KSC meeting material uses both Cr and Clr as councillor-title abbreviations. Treat them as observed title variants, not different roles.

FYY/#### — KSC File Numbers use F-prefixed year-like syntax, but the leading F has not been authoritatively expanded. Do not silently rewrite F as "File" even though the value sits in a field labelled File Number.

items.description: EPA may mean NSW Environment Protection Authority, while historical KSC planning material can use EPA Act for the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979. Never conflate the two.
Historical environmental-zone references can be obsolete under the later C1-C4 conservation-zone nomenclature. Date-control is required.
Historical contribution terminology corresponds to current sections 7.11 / 7.12 respectively.
The date matters. Kempsey DCP 2013 and Kempsey DCP 2026 must not be treated as interchangeable.
In corporate planning, OP means Operational Plan. Elsewhere KSC uses the phrase Operational Policy as a policy classification. Do not assume the two are interchangeable.
KSC material contains both IWCM (Integrated Water Cycle Management) and the older IWCMS (Integrated Water Cycle Management Strategy). Preserve the form actually used by the source and date it.

KSC’s 2024-25 capital-project abbreviation table itself gives URR two meanings: Unsealed Rural Roads and Urban Roads Regional. Resolve from the specific project/road context; do not expand URR mechanically.
KSC road-class shorthand is internally dense: UR and URL are both shown as Urban Roads Local, while URR is source-ambiguous. Preserve the exact code found in the source and its date/project context.
KSC engineering drawings use CR for Crescent, while Council governance/meeting records use Cr for Councillor. Capitalisation and document context are therefore material to interpretation.
KSC uses both forms for the Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009. They are aliases, not different statutes. Preserve the exact form used by the source when quoting or indexing records.
